newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK democrat urges Britain to defend elected chamber.
newsitem.headline: HK democrat urges Britain to defend elected chamber.

text.p: The leader of Hong Kong's Democratic Party urged Britain on Monday to defend the territory's elected legislature and to challenge in court China's plans to replace it after the handover next year.

"I think the least...the British government could do is to say very clearly the setting up of a provisional legislature is against the Joint Declaration and the Basic Law," said Martin Lee, chairman of the Democratic Party, on government radio on Monday.

"And that the British government in Hong Kong will take the provisional legislature to court if such a body were to be set up," Lee said, relating on radio issues that he discussed with Hong Kong governor Chris Patten during an earlier meeting.

China has vowed to dismantle the present fully-elected legislature next year in retaliation for a string of democratic reforms implemented unilaterally by colonial governor Chris Patten, and put in its place a provisional legislature.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, 1997.

It has been promised a high degree of autonomy under a "one-country, two systems" formula for the next 50 years under the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration and the Basic Law, a mini-constitution that will take effect next July 1.

But the territory of 6.3 million is weighed down by uncertainty over Beijing's intention to replace the elected legislature with a provisional one and threats to water down the territory's human rights bill.
Lee warned the provisional legislature which China intends to set up would not protect human rights and freedoms, and would destroy all hopes of an accountable government, the radio said.

Lee also appealed to Patten to give guidelines on the type of assistance to be provided by top government officials to the post-handover leader, to ensure that they do not give indirect assistance to the provisional legislature.
